newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan says Afghan victory would not end conflict.
newsitem.headline: Annan says Afghan victory would not end conflict.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Thursday that even if one side in civil war-torn Afghanistan took control of the entire country the conflict would not be over.

Answering a question at a news conference, he said: "We believe that there is no military solution to the situation in Afghanistan. And even if one party were to take the entire country, it does not mean that the quarrel is over.

"There are other minority elements within the society that will continue to resist from within and without. And this is why we have been trying to get the parties to accept a broad-based government and power-sharing, to be able to bring peace to Afghanistan."

Annan, who did not refer by name to the Moslem fundamentalist Taleban who control most of the country, including Kabul, the capital, said the head of the U.N. special mission to Afghanistan, Norbert Holl of Germany, had worked tirelessly to bring the parties together.
"Where the parties do not want to cooperate and are determined to find a solution on the battlefield, there is very little Dr. Holl or anyone can do," he said.
